description.narrative: Hostilities in the Middle East have affected the Gulf countries, placing areas under UNESCO’s mandate, including education systems and cultural heritage, water security and youth well-being under heightened strain. Infrastructures disruptions reverberate across the education sector by limiting access to physical learning environments for children and students, straining cultural institutions that support educational programming (such as museums and archives), and diverting national capacities away from educational development toward emergency response. It also threatens cultural heritage, traditional practices and cultural institutions of global value In this context, the UNESCO Office to the Gulf States and Yemen proposes a set of rapid initiatives aimed at strengthening regional cooperation, supporting national authorities, and mobilizing available technical expertise across UNESCO’s Sectors. Recognizing that crises disproportionately affect women and girls, the specific needs and priorities of women and girls will be systematically addressed throughout these programmes. These priority actions include enhanced coordination among Ministries of Education on online teaching tools and good practices, the assessment of risks to water and desalination systems as well as related mitigation measures, capacity building for museums and cultural institutions on risks preparedness, rapid social impact assessments, the implementation of psychosocial support measures for youth, social workers, psychologists and education personnel (with focus on women), as well as training sessions on the safety and freedom of scientists in emergency contexts.
